grades.quote: 1 indicates support for hardware Cache coherent DMA
grades.reason: This is part of the LoongArch CPUCFG feature-discovery table, which is a mechanism for discovering what the processor supports. Word 3 mostly lists microarchitectural and memory-system features such as cache-coherent DMA, LL/SC behavior, page-walk and performance counters. It has little on instruction-set support or processor identity, so it only helps a little.

This LoongArch CPUCFG word 2 table gives feature bits that show which instruction sets and extensions are supported. They include FP, LSX, LASX, the LBT binary-translation extensions, LAM atomics, FRECIPE and others. That directly answers how software discovers supported instructions.
This passage is about choosing PMLEN for pointer masking. It has nothing to do with discovering processor identity or supported instruction sets.
This passage describes atomicity physical memory attributes for an address region. It is not a way to discover processor identity or supported instruction sets.
